author: BBC News
description:
Prince Harry has received an enthusiastic welcome in a surprise visit to Ukraine to support injured war veterans, meeting Ukrainian competitors taking part in his Invictus Games.

There were emotional scenes as the Duke of Sussex was applauded by injured service men and women in Lviv, where he told his audience: "You're going to win the war."

Prince Harry spent two days at events for veterans, with a press blackout for security reasons until he had left Ukraine, as the country continues to face missile attacks from Russia.

Ukraine has more than 150,000 injured war veterans and the prince visited projects supporting their treatment and rehabilitation.

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Sean Coughlan.

description:
Today, we hear from Sunday Times chief news correspondent Rosamund Urwin, who was one of the journalists to break the Russell Brand story. 

She’s been talking to Mia Latter, who’s waived her legal right to anonymity to discuss allegations that Brand raped her when she was 16, and call for a law change around the age of consent. 

Latter’s allegations were not part of Brand's recent criminal trial, in which he was convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault, but he had denied Latter’s allegations before that. 

We also hear more from Alan Milburn ahead of the publication of his review into out of work and training young people, and look ahead to a week in which a UK-EU deal could be agreed.

description:
What would you tell an alien civilisation about life on Earth?

In 1977, a once-in-a-lifetime alignment of the planets gave Nasa the chance to launch spacecraft that could explore the outer edges of our solar system and beyond. Onboard was a gold-plated record carrying sounds, music and pictures of Earth, designed as a message for any aliens that might be out there. As the Voyager 1 probe reaches the milestone of one light-day from Earth, we explore the extraordinary story of the Golden Record. We look at how an alien civilisation might decode it, what its message reveals about humanity and how its map could point extraterrestrials back to our planet.

author: BBC News
description:
Environmental activists have long been committed to non-violent protest, but as global emissions continue to rise climate scholar Andreas Malm thinks they should change their tactics. 

The author of "How to Blow Up a Pipeline", who was recently refused entry to the UK, thinks the destruction and sabotage of fossil fuel infrastructure is now a legitimate and necessary weapon in the fight against climate change.

But can such illegal acts be justified, and how do you convince activists to commit them, risking lengthy prison sentences in the process? Plus, would destruction garner support or resentment from everyone else?

author: BBC News
description:
Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
 
Before settling into a sanctuary in 2015, the 11-year-old ape spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, Africa.
 
He was taken from the wild as an infant, and his family had been killed by the poachers who took him.
 
Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon now want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with.

author: BBC News
description:
After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto is back. GTA 6's launch is just around the corner, and the anticipation and hype has reached fever pitch. 
 
Tech Now's Laura Cress goes back to the place where the very first GTA was made in Dundee in Scotland and speaks to Dave Jones, the original game's co-creator and Brian Baglow, its publicist and writer, about how they created a global cultural phenomenon. 
 
And as we approach what's expected to be the biggest video game launch in history, Guardian video games editor Keza Macdonald explains just how big a moment for the industry the release of the latest game could be.
